targets.authors: Buccino G., Riggio L., Melli G., Binkofski F., Gallese V., Rizzolatti G.
targets.title: Listening to action-related sentences modulates the activity of the motor system: a combined TMS and behavioural study.
targets.evidence_quote: The target of this replication study is a seminal paper in the field of embodied language processing published by Buccino et al. ( 2005 ) that combined TMS and behavioral techniques.
targets.outcome_quote: As expected for hand stimulation, our data showed an early modulation of MEPs, according to the congruency between the linguistically described actions and the stimulated effector. This early modulation is consistent with the data from the original study and supports the idea of an early involvement of the motor system in language processing. However, the direction of the effect is reversed with respect to Buccino et al. ( 2005 ), where an interference effect was shown. Namely, hand MEPs increased in response to hand-related action sentences, as compared to foot-related and abstract ones.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly agree with original early hand motor modulation but contrast its reversed direction. Behavioral interaction did not replicate. Foot component was underpowered, but authors do not declare the entire attempt uninformative. No overall replication verdict outweighs the stated agreement and contrast.
